target_task.text: The combination targets the translation of natural language queries into executable SQL queries to enable structured data access for users without database expertise.

limitation.text: Direct generation methods often struggle with complex schemas, ambiguous column references, and multi-step reasoning, frequently resulting in syntax errors or incorrect semantic mappings when processing user questions.

combination.text: The approach combines a GPT model with specialized agentic or planning pipelines to process natural language queries, thereby improving schema exploration, iterative refinement, and the accuracy of generated text-to-sql expressions.

summary.text: This opportunity briefing explores combining GPT models with natural language queries and text-to-sql translation techniques to improve structured data access. As indicated by dvf:16, the design achieves a D score of 3.0 and an F score of 4.0, while V is missing. The system uses natural language inputs, processes them via a GPT backbone, and generates executable database queries.

target_user.text: The target users are developers and data analysts who deploy agentic AI data products and enterprise applications using open-source packages such as pkg:dbgpt and repositories like repo:eosphoros-ai/db-gpt.

jtbd.text: When users need to retrieve information from complex databases without writing manual code, they want to submit natural language inquiries so that the system translates them into valid, executable SQL queries.

value_prop.text: The combination democratizes access to structured databases by automating query translation, handling multi-step reasoning, and reducing syntax errors compared to manual writing.

riskiest_assumption.text: The riskiest assumption is designated due to missing evidence on axis V (viability) in dvf:16. Specifically, we assume that enterprise customers are willing to pay for an automated text-to-sql agentic assistant despite potential accuracy degradation on complex schemas.

mvp.text: To test the riskiest assumption regarding commercial viability, we will conduct customer interviews and price acceptance tests with prospective enterprise buyers. We will present a mockup of the DB-GPT agentic workflow and measure willingness to pay under a proposed threshold of 500 dollars per month, referencing dvf:16.
mvp.type: customer interviews and price acceptance test

success_metric.text: The success metric for the MVP is achieving a positive price acceptance rate of at least a proposed threshold of 40 percent among interviewed enterprise data teams, as motivated by dvf:16.

kill_criteria.text: Kill the project if fewer than a proposed threshold of 15 percent of interviewed customers express willingness to pay for the proposed tier, as indicated by dvf:16.

open_source.use: Used as the core repository for building agentic AI data products and managing database interactions.
Used as the base package to provide underlying data assistant capabilities and framework utilities.

to_build.text: Build a specialized billing and subscription management module to conduct price acceptance testing for enterprise customers, motivated by dvf:16.
